audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed as Elihu's entrance: friends stop answering, Elihu's anger at Job and the friends, youth/age wisdom tension, spirit/breath as source of understanding, and his compulsion to speak. Marked as Elihu's speech frame, not final theology.

verses.restored: These three men stopped answering Job, because he was righteous in his own eyes.

familiar.text: So these three men ceased to answer Job, because he was righteous in his own eyes.

modern.text: So these three men stopped answering Job, because he was righteous in his own eyes.

original.text: וַֽיִּשְׁבְּת֡וּ שְׁלֹ֤שֶׁת הָאֲנָשִׁ֣ים הָ֭אֵלֶּה מֵעֲנ֣וֹת אֶת אִיּ֑וֹב כִּ֤י ה֖וּא צַדִּ֣יק בְּעֵינָֽיו

verses.restored: Then the anger of Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite, from the clan of Ram, burned. Against Job his anger burned because he justified himself rather than the Divine.

familiar.text: Then was kindled the wrath of Elihu the son of Barachel the Buzite, of the kindred of Ram: against Job was his wrath kindled, because he justified himself rather than God.

modern.text: This kindled the anger of Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite, of the family of Ram. He burned with anger against Job for justifying himself rather than God,

original.text: וַיִּ֤חַר אַ֨ף אֱלִיה֣וּא בֶן בַּרַכְאֵ֣ל הַבּוּזִי֮ מִמִּשְׁפַּ֪חַ֫ת רָ֥ם בְּ֭אִיּוֹב חָרָ֣ה אַפּ֑וֹ עַֽל צַדְּק֥וֹ נַ֝פְשׁ֗וֹ מֵאֱלֹהִֽים

verses.restored: Against his three friends his anger also burned, because they had found no answer and yet had declared Job guilty.

familiar.text: Also against his three friends was his wrath kindled, because they had found no answer, and yet had condemned Job.

modern.text: and he burned with anger against Job’s three friends because they had failed to refute Job, and yet had condemned him.

original.text: וּבִשְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת רֵעָיו֮ חָרָ֪ה אַ֫פּ֥וֹ עַ֤ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹא מָצְא֣וּ מַעֲנֶ֑ה וַ֝יַּרְשִׁ֗יעוּ אֶת אִיּֽוֹב

verses.restored: Elihu had waited to speak to Job because they were older than he.

familiar.text: Now Elihu had waited till Job had spoken, because they were elder than he.

modern.text: Now Elihu had waited to speak to Job because the others were older than he.

original.text: וֶֽאֱלִיה֗וּ חִכָּ֣ה אֶת אִ֭יּוֹב בִּדְבָרִ֑ים כִּ֤י זְֽקֵנִים הֵ֖מָּה מִמֶּ֣נּוּ לְיָמִֽים

verses.restored: When Elihu saw that there was no answer in the mouth of the three men, his anger burned.

familiar.text: When Elihu saw that there was no answer in the mouth of these three men, then his wrath was kindled.

modern.text: But when he saw that the three men had no further reply, his anger was kindled.

original.text: וַיַּ֤רְא אֱלִיה֗וּא כִּ֘י אֵ֤ין מַעֲנֶ֗ה בְּ֭פִי שְׁלֹ֥שֶׁת הָאֲנָשִׁ֗ים וַיִּ֥חַר אַפּֽוֹ

verses.restored: Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite answered and said: I am young in days, and you are aged; therefore I held back and feared to declare my knowledge to you.

familiar.text: And Elihu the son of Barachel the Buzite answered and said, I am young, and ye are very old; wherefore I was afraid, and durst not shew you mine opinion.

modern.text: So Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite declared: “I am young in years, while you are old; that is why I was timid and afraid to tell you what I know.

original.text: וַיַּ֤עַן אֱלִיה֖וּא בֶן בַּֽרַכְאֵ֥ל הַבּוּזִ֗י וַיֹּ֫אמַ֥ר צָ֘עִ֤יר אֲנִ֣י לְ֭יָמִים וְאַתֶּ֣ם יְשִׁישִׁ֑ים עַל כֵּ֖ן זָחַ֥לְתִּי וָֽאִירָ֓א מֵחַוֺּ֖ת דֵּעִ֣י אֶתְכֶֽם

verses.restored: I said, Days should speak, and many years should make wisdom known.

familiar.text: I said, Days should speak, and multitude of years should teach wisdom.

modern.text: I thought that age should speak, and many years should teach wisdom.

original.text: אָ֭מַרְתִּי יָמִ֣ים יְדַבֵּ֑רוּ וְרֹ֥ב שָׁ֝נִ֗ים יֹדִ֥יעוּ חָכְמָֽה

verses.restored: But truly it is a spirit in a mortal, the breath of Shaddai, that gives them understanding.

familiar.text: But there is a spirit in man: and the inspiration of the Almighty giveth them understanding.

modern.text: But there is a spirit in a man, the breath of the Almighty, that gives him understanding.

original.text: אָ֭כֵן רֽוּחַ הִ֣יא בֶאֱנ֑וֹשׁ וְנִשְׁמַ֖ת שַׁדַּ֣י תְּבִינֵֽם

verses.restored: It is not the great who are wise, nor do the aged understand justice.

familiar.text: Great men are not always wise: neither do the aged understand judgment.

modern.text: It is not only the old who are wise, or the elderly who understand justice.

original.text: לֹֽא רַבִּ֥ים יֶחְכָּ֑מוּ וּ֝זְקֵנִ֗ים יָבִ֥ינוּ מִשְׁפָּֽט

verses.restored: Therefore I say, Listen to me; I too will declare my knowledge.

familiar.text: Therefore I said, Hearken to me; I also will shew mine opinion.

modern.text: Therefore I say, ‘Listen to me; I too will declare what I know.’

original.text: לָכֵ֣ן אָ֭מַרְתִּי שִׁמְעָה לִּ֑י אֲחַוֶּ֖ה דֵּעִ֣י אַף אָֽנִי

verses.restored: Look, I waited for your words; I listened for your understandings while you searched out speeches.

familiar.text: Behold, I waited for your words; I gave ear to your reasons, whilst ye searched out what to say.

modern.text: Indeed, I waited while you spoke; I listened to your reasoning; as you searched for words,

original.text: הֵ֤ן הוֹחַ֨לְתִּי לְֽדִבְרֵיכֶ֗ם אָ֭זִין עַד תְּב֥וּנֹֽתֵיכֶ֑ם עַֽד תַּחְקְר֥וּן מִלִּֽין

verses.restored: I gave attention to you, and look, none of you refuted Job or answered his words.

familiar.text: Yea, I attended unto you, and, behold, there was none of you that convinced Job, or that answered his words:

modern.text: I paid you full attention. But no one proved Job wrong; not one of you rebutted his arguments.

original.text: וְעָֽדֵיכֶ֗ם אֶתְבּ֫וֹנָ֥ן וְהִנֵּ֤ה אֵ֣ין לְאִיּ֣וֹב מוֹכִ֑יחַ עוֹנֶ֖ה אֲמָרָ֣יו מִכֶּֽם

verses.restored: Do not say, We have found wisdom; the Divine will defeat him, not a man.

familiar.text: Lest ye should say, We have found out wisdom: God thrusteth him down, not man.

modern.text: So do not claim, ‘We have found wisdom; let God, not man, refute him.’

original.text: פֶּן תֹּ֣֭אמְרוּ מָצָ֣אנוּ חָכְמָ֑ה אֵ֖ל יִדְּפֶ֣נּוּ לֹא אִֽישׁ

verses.restored: He has not arranged words against me, and with your sayings I will not answer him.

familiar.text: Now he hath not directed his words against me: neither will I answer him with your speeches.

modern.text: But Job has not directed his words against me, and I will not answer him with your arguments.

original.text: וְלֹא עָרַ֣ךְ אֵלַ֣י מִלִּ֑ין וּ֝בְאִמְרֵיכֶ֗ם לֹ֣א אֲשִׁיבֶֽנּוּ

verses.restored: They are dismayed; they answer no more; words have departed from them.

familiar.text: They were amazed, they answered no more: they left off speaking.

modern.text: Job’s friends are dismayed, with no more to say; words have escaped them.

original.text: חַ֭תּוּ לֹא עָ֣נוּ ע֑וֹד הֶעְתִּ֖יקוּ מֵהֶ֣ם מִלִּֽים

verses.restored: Shall I wait because they do not speak, because they stand still and answer no more?

familiar.text: When I had waited, (for they spake not, but stood still, and answered no more;)

modern.text: Must I wait, now that they are silent, now that they stand and no longer reply?

original.text: וְ֭הוֹחַלְתִּי כִּי לֹ֣א יְדַבֵּ֑רוּ כִּ֥י עָ֝מְד֗וּ לֹא עָ֥נוּ עֽוֹד

verses.restored: I too will answer my share; I too will declare my knowledge.

familiar.text: I said, I will answer also my part, I also will shew mine opinion.

modern.text: I too will answer; yes, I will declare what I know.

original.text: אַעֲנֶ֣ה אַף אֲנִ֣י חֶלְקִ֑י אֲחַוֶּ֖ה דֵעִ֣י אַף אָֽנִי

verses.restored: For I am full of words; the spirit within me presses me.

familiar.text: For I am full of matter, the spirit within me constraineth me.

modern.text: For I am full of words, and my spirit within me compels me.

original.text: כִּ֭י מָלֵ֣תִי מִלִּ֑ים הֱ֝צִיקַ֗תְנִי ר֣וּחַ בִּטְנִֽי

verses.restored: Look, my belly is like wine not opened, like new wineskins ready to burst.

familiar.text: Behold, my belly is as wine which hath no vent; it is ready to burst like new bottles.

modern.text: Behold, my belly is like unvented wine; it is about to burst like a new wineskin.

original.text: הִנֵּֽה בִטְנִ֗י כְּיַ֥יִן לֹא יִפָּתֵ֑חַ כְּאֹב֥וֹת חֲ֝דָשִׁ֗ים יִבָּקֵֽעַ

verses.restored: I will speak, that there may be relief for me; I will open my lips and answer.

familiar.text: I will speak, that I may be refreshed: I will open my lips and answer.

modern.text: I must speak and find relief; I must open my lips and respond.

original.text: אֲדַבְּרָ֥ה וְיִֽרְוַֽח לִ֑י אֶפְתַּ֖ח שְׂפָתַ֣י וְאֶֽעֱנֶֽה

verses.restored: Please let me not show partiality to anyone, nor flatter any human.

familiar.text: Let me not, I pray you, accept any man’s person, neither let me give flattering titles unto man.

modern.text: I will be partial to no one, nor will I flatter any man.

original.text: אַל נָ֭א אֶשָּׂ֣א פְנֵי אִ֑ישׁ וְאֶל אָ֝דָ֗ם לֹ֣א אֲכַנֶּֽה

verses.restored: For I do not know how to flatter; soon my Maker would take me away.

familiar.text: For I know not to give flattering titles; in so doing my maker would soon take me away.

modern.text: For I do not know how to flatter, or my Maker would remove me in an instant.

original.text: כִּ֤י לֹ֣א יָדַ֣עְתִּי אֲכַנֶּ֑ה כִּ֝מְעַ֗ט יִשָּׂאֵ֥נִי עֹשֵֽׂנִי
